title: D-004: Multi-Tool Wrapper Architecture
body:
# D-004: Multi-Tool Wrapper Architecture

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Active

## Decision

Support Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Windsurf, and GitHub Copilot via thin per-tool wrapper directories (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.windsurf/`, `.copilot/`). Each wrapper adapts `.writing-framework/` content to the tool's native format.

## Why

Locking the framework to one AI tool defeats the portability goal. Each tool has a different convention for loading persistent instructions and invoking commands — Claude Code uses `.claude/commands/*.md`, Windsurf uses `.windsurfrules`, Copilot uses `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. The wrapper design lets each tool use its native mechanism while sharing the same canonical content.

The wrapper architecture enforces a design discipline: all substantive content must live in `.writing-framework/`, not in the tool adapter files. This means adding a new supported tool requires only creating a new thin adapter directory — the commands, agents, doctrine, and schemas do not need to be duplicated.

## Design Rule

Wrappers are thin. A Claude Code command file in `.claude/commands/` references `.writing-framework/commands/[name].md` — it does not redefine the command. All substantive content lives in `.writing-framework/`. If a wrapper file contains more than a brief description and a reference to the canonical spec, it is violating the thin wrapper principle.

## Alternatives Considered

**One universal format that all tools read.** Rejected: no such format exists and requiring a specific tool to adapt would reduce adoption. Each tool team maintains their own loading conventions and there is no industry-standard format for persistent agent instructions.

**Separate full copies per tool.** Rejected: creates divergence. If the brief-writer spec changes, it must be updated in `.writing-framework/` and also in four tool-specific copies. The single-source principle (D-010) prohibits this.

## Consequences

Changes to a command spec in `.writing-framework/commands/` propagate to all tools without changing the wrapper files. Wrappers only need updating when a tool's native format changes. When a tool is deprecated or a new tool is added, only the wrapper directory is affected — the canonical framework content is untouched. This architecture also means the framework can be validated independently of any specific tool: the `.writing-framework/` content is the system, and the wrappers are merely translation layers.
